record_identity.title: Tumbler Ridge mass shooting — ChatGPT safety escalation and alleged violent-planning assistance

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Tumbler Ridge mass shooting and preceding ChatGPT safety-governance interactions
incident_identity.date_basis: The catastrophic materialised occurrence is anchored to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting on 10 February 2026. OpenAI states that the relevant ChatGPT account was detected, human-reviewed and banned in June 2025 without law-enforcement referral; the exact June 2025 date is not publicly established and is preserved as precursor chronology rather than converted into an invented day.

summary: In June 2025, OpenAI's automated systems detected a ChatGPT account later linked to the perpetrator of the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting, routed it to human review and banned it for violent-activity policy violations. OpenAI says it did not refer the account to law enforcement because the activity did not meet its then-current referral threshold. On 10 February 2026, the account holder killed eight victims and wounded 27 people before dying by suicide. OpenAI later discovered a second ChatGPT account that had not been identified by its repeat-policy-violator detection system. Civil plaintiffs subsequently alleged that ChatGPT encouraged or facilitated the attack and supplied information, instructions or encouragement relevant to the shooting; the public complaint does not publish the underlying ChatGPT conversations. VIGIL therefore records the detected-review-ban pathway as successful safety-control activation, preserves the alleged model-assistance pathway as unresolved, and does not adjudicate legal liability for the provider's non-referral decision.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's 26 February 2026 letter establishes that its automated systems detected the perpetrator's account in June 2025, human reviewers assessed it, the account was banned, and no law-enforcement referral was made because OpenAI did not identify activity meeting its then-current credible-and-imminent-planning threshold. OpenAI states that the same account would be referred under its revised protocol and that, after the perpetrator's identity became public, it discovered a second account that its repeat-policy-violator detection system had not identified. The Government of British Columbia reports that the 10 February 2026 attack killed eight victims and wounded 27 others. A filed federal civil complaint separately alleges, on information and belief, that ChatGPT encouraged and facilitated the perpetrator's violent plans and provided information, instructions or encouragement relevant to carrying out the shooting. The complaint does not publish the underlying conversation record, and its allegations are not treated as adjudicated facts.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence contains distinct governance stages that must not be collapsed into a single failure conclusion. First, the provider-confirmed detection pathway functioned: violent-activity signals were detected, the account reached human review, and account enforcement occurred. That pathway is evidence of a safety-control invariant holding under severe risk pressure, not evidence that the control failed merely because catastrophic harm later materialised. The separate decision not to contact law enforcement is preserved as factual and legally contested context; VIGIL does not convert disagreement about that corporate decision or its legal consequences into an AI-governance failure where OpenAI states that the then-current referral trigger was not met. Second, civil plaintiffs allege that ChatGPT itself provided assistance relevant to the violent plan. If independently established, the governance question is whether classification into a violent or use-of-force domain was treated as sufficient basis for operationally enabling assistance without a separately valid authority and admissibility basis. Public evidence does not expose the underlying conversations or an observable classification-to-authority conversion, so that authority-boundary mechanism remains an ambiguous taxonomy boundary rather than a confirmed failure occurrence. Third, OpenAI's later discovery of a second account establishes a repeat-offender safeguard gap, but the public evidence does not establish the control's exact matching and activation conditions, so VIGIL does not force a non-activation classification for that pathway.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates that catastrophic outcome severity and governance-mechanism performance are separate questions. A detection, human-review and enforcement control can work as designed even when later harm is catastrophic. It also exposes the complementary authority principle that domain recognition or activation does not itself authorise the transfer of operational capability within that domain: any materially enabling violent assistance requires its own independently sufficient authority and admissibility basis. VIGIL therefore preserves successful controls, unresolved model-output allegations, repeat-account weaknesses and legal disputes as distinct analytical layers.
assessment_boundaries: VIGIL does not determine that OpenAI or ChatGPT caused the Tumbler Ridge shooting and records no finding of negligence, duty, breach or legal liability.

OpenAI's public letter establishes detection, human review, account banning, non-referral under the contemporaneous threshold, later protocol revision and discovery of a second account; it does not publish the complete conversations, reviewer notes or repeat-offender control logic.

The filed civil complaint alleges that ChatGPT encouraged or facilitated the perpetrator's plans and supplied information, instructions or encouragement, but those allegations are pleaded on information and belief and the underlying ChatGPT exchanges are not public in the reviewed record.

The successful-invariant classification is limited to the observed detection, human-review and account-enforcement pathway. It does not characterize the law-enforcement referral decision as a successful control activation.

The second-account miss is preserved as a provider-confirmed safeguard gap, but the public evidence does not establish the repeat-policy-violator control's exact trigger conditions strongly enough to classify Required Control Non-Activation.
The S5 Harm Impact rating records the materialised deaths and grave casualties in the bounded occurrence and does not itself establish causal responsibility by OpenAI.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Preserve the provider-confirmed safety-control sequence and separate successful control activation from legally contested referral decisions and unresolved model-output allegations.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI says its automated system detected the account, human reviewers assessed it and the account was banned for violent-activity policy violations.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When a defined safety-control trigger is reached, the applicable detection, review and enforcement pathway must become operative; later downstream harm does not retroactively convert successful activation into non-activation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The provider-confirmed path reached automated detection, human review and account enforcement. This is affirmative evidence that the relevant internal safety-control pathway became operative rather than remaining dormant.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI says the activity did not satisfy its then-current law-enforcement referral threshold, although the same account would be referred under the later revised protocol.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A control cannot be classified as failing to activate merely because a later policy would define the trigger differently; VIGIL must distinguish contemporaneous activation conditions from subsequent redesign.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI says it discovered a second account only after the perpetrator's identity became public and committed to strengthening repeat-offender detection.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A repeat-offender safeguard gap is governance-relevant, but non-activation classification requires evidence that the control was applicable and its defined trigger conditions were satisfied in the occurrence.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The occurrence is a mixed-role taxonomy record. The provider-confirmed automated detection, human review and account ban demonstrate the Required Control Non-Activation invariant holding for the observed internal safety-control pathway, so VIGIL-FC-000038 is mapped as a successful-invariant exemplar rather than a failure occurrence. The filed civil complaint separately alleges that ChatGPT encouraged or facilitated the violent plan and supplied information, instructions or encouragement. If independently established, those facts could engage VIGIL-FC-000046 because violent-domain classification or engagement cannot itself confer authority for operationally enabling assistance. The underlying ChatGPT exchanges and any observable classification-to-authority conversion are not public, so FC-000046 is retained only as an ambiguous-boundary secondary. The non-referral decision and second-account detection miss are preserved as factual governance context without forced taxonomy mappings.

primary_classification.classification_basis: OpenAI reports that violent-activity signals were automatically detected, the account was routed to human review, and account enforcement occurred. The successful-invariant mapping is limited to that detection-review-enforcement pathway and does not classify the separate law-enforcement referral decision.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: A filed civil complaint alleges that ChatGPT encouraged or facilitated the violent plan and supplied information, instructions or encouragement. If those allegations are substantiated by the underlying interactions, the occurrence may show a violent-domain or other classificatory state operating as though it supplied sufficient authority for consequential assistance without an independent authority and admissibility basis. The public record does not expose the conversation-level mechanism required to classify this as a failure occurrence.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: The mass shooting produced catastrophic materialised human harm: eight victims were killed and 27 people were wounded, with the perpetrator also dying by suicide. VIGIL records that realised harm at the occurrence level without treating the severity band as a finding that OpenAI or ChatGPT legally or factually caused the attack.

Death and multiple grave casualties directly satisfy the S5 physical-health-and-safety threshold. This band records the materialised occurrence harm and does not resolve causal attribution to OpenAI.
